name: Post-Money Valuation and Investor Ownership
description: Gives the share of the company an investor receives: investment divided by post-money valuation (pre-money plus investment).
notes: Here 20 % of a 10,000,000 post-money company.

name: Founder Dilution after a Round
description: Gives an existing holder's ownership after new shares are issued in a priced round.
notes: The value of the stake does not fall if the round is priced fairly; only the percentage does.

name: Venture Capital Method: Required Ownership
description: Gives the stake a venture investor needs today so that the expected exit delivers the target return.
notes: Adjust further for dilution from later rounds.

name: Liquidation Preference Payout
description: Gives what a holder of non-participating preferred stock receives at exit: the larger of the preference and its converted share, capped at the exit value.
notes: At a 20,000,000 exit the 1× preference (5,000,000) beats a 20 % share (4,000,000).

name: Total Value to Paid-In (TVPI)
description: Gives a private fund's total value created per unit of capital paid in (realised plus unrealised).
notes: DPI (distributions/paid-in) is the realised part, RVPI (NAV/paid-in) the unrealised part.

name: Kaplan–Schoar Public Market Equivalent (PME)
expression: (sum(dist / idx) + nav_end / at(idx, len(idx))) / sum(calls / idx)
description: Compares a private fund with a public index: index-adjusted distributions (plus final NAV) over index-adjusted contributions (Kaplan and Schoar 2005).
notes: Above 1 means the fund beat the index.

name: Performance Fee above a High-Water Mark
description: Charges a performance fee only on gains above the highest previous NAV, so investors never pay twice for the same gains.
notes: Many funds add a hurdle rate on top.

name: "2 and 20" Fund Fees
expression: aum * mf + max(prof - hr * aum, 0) * pf
description: Adds a management fee on assets and a performance fee on profits above a hurdle (hard-hurdle version).
notes: Here 2,000,000 + 2,000,000 = 4,000,000, eating over a quarter of the gross profit.

name: Cost of a Fund Expense Ratio over Time
description: Gives how much less an investment grows to because of a yearly expense ratio.
notes: A 1 % fee on 100,000 over 30 years costs about 187,000 at 7 %.

name: ETF Premium or Discount to NAV
description: Gives how far an exchange-traded fund or closed-end fund trades above (premium) or below (discount) its net asset value.
notes: Closed-end funds can trade at persistent discounts of 10 % or more.

name: Distributions to Paid-In (DPI)
description: Computes DPI, the cash returned to a fund's investors as a multiple of the capital they have paid in.
notes: DPI counts only cash actually returned; TVPI also counts the remaining value (RVPI = TVPI − DPI).

name: Price per Share in a Priced Round

variables.label: Fully diluted shares before the round

description: Computes the price per share in a funding round from the pre-money valuation and the fully diluted shares before the round.
notes: Fully diluted shares include options and the option pool; what is counted is set in the term sheet.

name: Shares Issued in a Priced Round

variables.label: Fully diluted shares before the round

description: Computes the number of new shares issued to investors: the amount invested divided by the price per share.
notes: The price per share is the pre-money valuation divided by the fully diluted shares.

name: Post-Money SAFE Ownership
description: Computes the ownership a post-money SAFE converts into at the valuation cap.
notes: With the post-money SAFE (Y Combinator, 2018) the investor's share is fixed before the priced round, which then dilutes it.

name: Convertible Note Conversion Price

variables.label: Price per share in the round

description: Computes the price at which a convertible note or SAFE with both a cap and a discount converts: the lower of the cap price and the discounted round price.
notes: Accrued interest on a note is added to the amount converted. How the cap price is computed depends on the agreement.

name: Effective Pre-Money after an Option Pool Increase
description: Computes the effective pre-money valuation when investors require a new option pool to be created before the round (the option pool shuffle).
notes: The pool comes out of the existing holders' share, so the founders' valuation is lower than the headline figure.

name: Net Asset Value per Unit
description: Computes a fund's net asset value per unit or share.
notes: Accrued fees and expenses are part of the liabilities.

name: Amount Invested after a Front-End Load
description: Computes the amount actually invested in a fund after a front-end sales charge is taken.
notes: The load is a percentage of the amount paid (the offering price), not of the amount invested.

name: Pro Rata Investment to Keep Ownership
description: Computes how much an existing investor must put into a new round to keep the same ownership.
notes: Pro rata rights are agreed in the investment documents and may be limited.

name: Carried Interest with a Hurdle and Full Catch-Up
description: Computes the general partner's carried interest in a whole-fund waterfall with a preferred return and a 100 % catch-up.
notes: Investors first get their capital back and the preferred return; the manager then takes everything until it has its share of all profit.

name: Participating Preferred Payout
expression: min(mult * amt, exitv) + own / 100 * max(exitv - mult * amt, 0)
description: Computes the payout to a participating preferred investor: the liquidation preference plus its share of what remains.
notes: There is no cap on participation here; other preferred classes and debt are ignored.
